FeatherDesk API reference

Self-hosted, lightweight help desk. Version 1.2.0. Every operation below with its parameters, request body, responses and copy-ready examples.

Machine-readable spec. The full OpenAPI 3.1 document is at /api/v1/openapi.yaml — import it into Postman, Insomnia or Bruno, or generate a client with openapi-generator / oapi-codegen / openapi-typescript.

FeatherDesk REST API (v1). One API serves the SPA and integrations.

Path convention. Paths below are relative to the server URL /api/v1 (e.g. /auth/config is GET /api/v1/auth/config). A few routes live at the site root and carry a path-level servers: [{url: /}] override: /healthz, /readyz, /metrics, /branding/{file}, /kb/sitemap.xml, /api/docs, /manifest.webmanifest, /mcp.

Authentication. Either the session cookie fd_session (browser; cookie-authenticated POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE must send X-CSRF-Token with the value from GET /me) or Authorization: Bearer fd_pat_… (personal access token). Required PAT scopes are listed per operation in x-scopes; effective permission is the owner's role ∩ token scopes.

Errors are RFC 9457 application/problem+json (Problem). Reads of objects outside the caller's visibility return 404; actions on visible objects the caller may not perform return 403.

Pagination is cursor-based: ?limit=50&cursor=… → {items, next_cursor}.

Realtime. GET /ws upgrades to a WebSocket (subprotocol featherdesk.v1); see x-websocket on that operation and the WsClientFrame/WsServerFrame schemas. Mutations always go through REST.

Webhooks are described in the top-level webhooks section. Delivery is at-least-once: deduplicate on the envelope id.

Sections: Authentication · Errors · Webhooks · System · Auth · Setup · Me · Realtime · Portal · Tickets · Projects · Directory · Reports · Knowledge base · Inbound email · Branding · Administration · Privacy · MCP · Integrations

Authentication

MethodHowUse it for
Personal access tokenAuthorization: Bearer fd_pat_…. Create one under Profile → API tokens and choose its scopes. The token can do what its owner can, limited to the scopes listed on each operation.Scripts, integrations, CI, AI assistants
Session cookieThe fd_session cookie set at sign-in. Every POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE must also send X-CSRF-Token with the csrf_token value from GET /api/v1/me.The web app, browser-based tools

Quick start

export FD=https://help.example.com
export TOKEN=fd_pat_…   # Profile → API tokens

curl "$FD/api/v1/me" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

curl -X POST "$FD/api/v1/agent/tickets" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Idempotency-Key: 6f1c2b0e' \
  -d '{"subject":"VPN drops every 10 minutes","body_md":"Since this morning…","requester_email":"ada@example.com"}'

Operations marked public need no authentication. Paths under /api/v1/agent are for staff, /api/v1/portal for customers and /api/v1/admin for administrators; other users get 404.

Requests and pagination

  • Base URL https://help.example.com/api/v1. Requests and responses are JSON (application/json, UTF-8) unless an operation says otherwise; timestamps are RFC 3339 in UTC; IDs are UUIDs.
  • Pagination: list operations take ?limit= (1–200, default 50) and return {"items": […], "next_cursor": "…"}; pass next_cursor back as ?cursor= until it is null.
  • Idempotency: create operations accept Idempotency-Key. Retrying with the same key within 24 h returns the first response instead of creating a duplicate; the same key with a different body is a 422.
  • Concurrency: ticket responses carry an ETag; send it as If-Match on PATCH to get 412 instead of overwriting someone else's change.
  • Rate limits: over the limit you get 429 with Retry-After (seconds).
  • Realtime: GET /api/v1/ws upgrades to a WebSocket (subprotocol featherdesk.v1) that pushes ticket changes; writes always go through REST.

Errors

Errors are RFC 9457 problem documents (application/problem+json). Branch on status and the type slug; title and detail are for humans. Objects you cannot see answer 404; actions you may not perform on objects you can see answer 403.

400 BadRequest

Malformed request

HTTP/1.1 400
Content-Type: application/problem+json

{
  "type": "https://featherdesk.dev/problems/bad-request",
  "title": "Bad request",
  "status": 400,
  "detail": "invalid JSON body"
}

401 Unauthenticated

Not authenticated (unauthenticated)

HTTP/1.1 401
Content-Type: application/problem+json

{
  "type": "https://featherdesk.dev/problems/unauthenticated",
  "title": "Authentication required",
  "status": 401
}

403 Forbidden

Visible but not allowed (forbidden, csrf): missing role for the route group, PAT without the operation's x-scopes, or a cookie mutation without a valid CSRF token

HTTP/1.1 403
Content-Type: application/problem+json

{
  "type": "https://featherdesk.dev/problems/forbidden",
  "title": "Forbidden",
  "status": 403
}

404 NotFound

Not found or not visible to the caller (not-found). Portal routes answer 404 to staff and agent/admin routes answer 404 to customers. portal-disabled: the customer portal is switched off (support.portal_enabled=false), so customer sign-in endpoints and the /portal/* group answer 404 to customers (a customer personal access token gets 404 there and 401 elsewhere)

HTTP/1.1 404
Content-Type: application/problem+json

{
  "type": "https://featherdesk.dev/problems/not-found",
  "title": "Not found",
  "status": 404
}

409 Conflict

Conflict (conflict, invalid-transition, merge-cross-requester, link-cycle, email-disabled, setup-required, idempotency-in-flight: a request with the same Idempotency-Key is still running)

HTTP/1.1 409
Content-Type: application/problem+json

{
  "type": "https://featherdesk.dev/problems/invalid-transition",
  "title": "Invalid status transition",
  "status": 409,
  "allowed": [
    "open",
    "pending"
  ]
}

412 PreconditionFailed

If-Match did not match (precondition-failed)

HTTP/1.1 412
Content-Type: application/problem+json

{
  "type": "https://featherdesk.dev/problems/precondition-failed",
  "title": "Precondition failed",
  "status": 412,
  "detail": "The ticket was changed by someone else."
}

413 TooLarge

Payload too large (payload-too-large)

HTTP/1.1 413
Content-Type: application/problem+json

{
  "type": "https://featherdesk.dev/problems/payload-too-large",
  "title": "Payload too large",
  "status": 413
}

422 Validation

Validation failed (validation, field-required, idempotency-mismatch)

HTTP/1.1 422
Content-Type: application/problem+json

{
  "type": "https://featherdesk.dev/problems/validation",
  "title": "Validation failed",
  "status": 422,
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "subject",
      "code": "required",
      "message": "This field is required."
    },
    {
      "field": "requester_email",
      "code": "email",
      "message": "Enter a valid email address."
    }
  ]
}

429 RateLimited

Too many requests (rate-limited)

HTTP/1.1 429
Content-Type: application/problem+json
Retry-After: 30

{
  "type": "https://featherdesk.dev/problems/rate-limited",
  "title": "Too many requests",
  "status": 429
}

503 Unavailable

A dependency is temporarily unavailable (unavailable): identity provider down, blob storage not configured, or the server is shutting down

HTTP/1.1 503
Content-Type: application/problem+json
Retry-After: 5

{
  "type": "https://featherdesk.dev/problems/unavailable",
  "title": "Service unavailable",
  "status": 503
}

POST/api/v1/auth/login#

Local login

public

Sets the fd_session cookie. Failures are constant-time and generic. With audience customer it answers 404 portal-disabled while support.portal_enabled is off. Staff local login only works for break-glass admins unless FD_AUTH_STAFF_LOCAL=true.

With two-factor authentication a correct password answers MfaChallenge instead and sets no cookie: continue with POST /auth/mfa/verify (or /auth/mfa/enroll/* when the security.mfa_required policy forces enrolment). The same applies to verify-email, magic-link and invite-accept. OIDC logins and personal access tokens are never challenged.

one of: staff, customer
emailrequiredstring (email)
passwordrequiredstring
min length 1 · max length 128

POST/api/v1/auth/mfa/verify#

Complete a login with a second factor

public

Second step of a login that answered MfaChallenge. method is one of the challenge's methods. Success sets the fd_session cookie and returns Me. A wrong code is a 422 on code while attempts remain (5 per challenge, each one also counts toward the login throttle); an unknown, used, expired or exhausted challenge is a 401 and the user signs in again. TOTP codes are accepted within ±1 step and never twice; recovery codes are single use.

Request body · application/json · required

FieldTypeDescription
mfa_tokenrequiredstring
min length 1 · max length 128
methodrequiredMfaMethod

Second factors. recovery is a single-use recovery code.

one of: totp, email, recovery
coderequiredstring
min length 1 · max length 64

Responses

200

OK

application/json · Me
401

Not authenticated (unauthenticated)

application/problem+json · Problem
Error format and example

application/problem+json · Problem
Error format and example
422

application/problem+json · Problem
Error format and example

GET/api/v1/auth/oidc/{audience}/start#

Start OIDC login

public

Staff audience in CORE, customer audience in V1. 404 when that audience has no OIDC client configured, or (customer audience) 404 portal-disabled while the customer portal is switched off.

Parameters

NameInTypeDescription
audiencerequiredpathAudience
one of: staff, customer
redirectquerystring

Same-origin path to return to after login

Responses

302

Redirect to the IdP (state, nonce, PKCE)

404

Not found or not visible to the caller (not-found). Portal routes answer 404 to staff and agent/admin routes answer 404 to customers. portal-disabled: the customer portal is switched off (support.portal_enabled=false), so customer sign-in endpoints and the /portal/* group answer 404 to customers (a customer personal access token gets 404 there and 401 elsewhere)

application/problem+json · Problem
Error format and example
503

A dependency is temporarily unavailable (unavailable): identity provider down, blob storage not configured, or the server is shutting down

application/problem+json · Problem
Headers: Retry-After
Error format and example

Request

curl 'https://help.example.com/api/v1/auth/oidc/staff/start'
GET/api/v1/auth/oidc/{audience}/callback#

OIDC callback

public

Verifies the ID token, syncs staff role/tier from groups on every login. No mapped group → 403 and the user is disabled.

The customer audience answers 404 portal-disabled while the customer portal is switched off.

A refused browser navigation (Accept: text/html) in the staff audience is redirected (302) to /agent/login?error=<code> instead, with code one of no_role, disabled, oidc_failed, idp_unavailable, so the login page can explain it.

Parameters

NameInTypeDescription
audiencerequiredpathAudience
one of: staff, customer
codequerystring
statequerystring

Responses

302

Redirect into the area with the session cookie set; or, for a refused staff browser login, to /agent/login?error=<code>

application/problem+json · Problem

503

GET/api/v1/me/notifications#

My in-app notifications

auth: token or session

Notification centre. Newest first, keyset-paginated. Rows are written by the notify consumer with the same recipients as email; the actor is never notified and customer rows carry only public data. POST/api/v1/portal/tickets/{id}/messages#

Reply

auth: token or sessiontickets:writeCustomers

Pending → open automatically. Replying to a closed ticket returns 409 with the follow-up ticket id in detail; use the follow-up.

Parameters

NameInTypeDescription
idrequiredpathstring

UUIDv7

Idempotency-Keyheaderstring

Replays within 24 h return the original response; a different body with the same key → 422 idempotency-mismatch

max length 200

Request body · application/json · required

FieldTypeDescription
body_mdrequiredstring
min length 1 · max length 65536
attachment_idsstring[]
max items 10

Responses

201

OK

application/json · CustomerMessage
401

Not authenticated (unauthenticated)

application/problem+json · Problem
Error format and example
403

Visible but not allowed (forbidden, csrf): missing role for the route group, PAT without the operation's x-scopes, or a cookie mutation without a valid CSRF token

application/problem+json · Problem
Error format and example
404

Not found or not visible to the caller (not-found). Portal routes answer 404 to staff and agent/admin routes answer 404 to customers. portal-disabled: the customer portal is switched off (support.portal_enabled=false), so customer sign-in endpoints and the /portal/* group answer 404 to customers (a customer personal access token gets 404 there and 401 elsewhere)

application/problem+json · Problem
Error format and example
409

Conflict (conflict, invalid-transition, merge-cross-requester, link-cycle, email-disabled, setup-required, idempotency-in-flight: a request with the same Idempotency-Key is still running)

application/problem+json · Problem
Error format and example
422

Validation failed (validation, field-required, idempotency-mismatch)

application/problem+json · Problem
Error format and example

Request

curl -X POST 'https://help.example.com/api/v1/portal/tickets/0192f3c4-5b6a-7c8d-9e0f-1a2b3c4d5e6f/messages' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer fd_pat_…' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"body_md":"Since this morning the VPN disconnects every ten minutes.","attachment_ids":["0192f3c4-5b6a-7c8d-9e0f-1a2b3c4d5e6f"]}'

Request body

{
  "body_md": "Since this morning the VPN disconnects every ten minutes.",
  "attachment_ids": [
    "0192f3c4-5b6a-7c8d-9e0f-1a2b3c4d5e6f"
  ]
}

PATCH/api/v1/portal/tickets/{id}/fields#

Edit my customer-editable custom fields

auth: token or sessiontickets:writeCustomers

Updates customer-editable custom field values while the ticket is not closed (409 when closed). Keys that are not customer-editable are rejected with 422 (cf.<key>: read_only; staff-only keys look unknown). Emits one ticket.fields_changed event.

Parameters

NameInTypeDescription
idrequiredpathstring

UUIDv7

Request body · application/json · required

FieldTypeDescription
custom_fieldsrequiredCustomFieldValues

Map of field key → value. Customer views contain only customer_visible fields.

200

OK

application/json · CustomerTicket
401

POST/api/v1/agent/tickets#

Create a ticket on behalf of a customer

auth: token or sessiontickets:writetickets:act_as_customerStaff

With a token holding tickets:act_as_customer the first message is authored by the requester, posted with channel: api and via_integration: true, audited as ticket.message.on_behalf, and the answer is the minimal CustomerTicketOnBehalfResult instead of the staff Ticket. team_id, assignee_id and tags then also need tickets:write (403); a disabled requester is 409 on-behalf-disabled. Such creates share the per-token limit of 60 per minute (burst 20, 429). Without that scope the first message is authored by the token or session owner, as before.

Parameters

NameInTypeDescription
Idempotency-Keyheaderstring

Replays within 24 h return the original response; a different body with the same key → 422 idempotency-mismatch

max length 200

Request body · application/json · required

FieldTypeDescription
subjectrequiredstring
min length 1 · max length 200
body_mdrequiredstring
min length 1 · max length 65536
requester_idstring | null
requester_emailstring (email)
requester_namestring
category_idstring | null
team_idstring | null
priorityPriority
one of: low, normal, high, urgent
assignee_idstring | null
attachment_idsstring[]
max items 10
custom_fieldsCustomFieldValues

Map of field key → value. Customer views contain only customer_visible fields.

tagsstring[]
project_idstring

Project id or key. Omitted: the category's project, else (customers) the only project open to them, else the default project. Customers need a portal-visible project their organization may use; agents need a membership (422 not_allowed).

max length 36

Responses

201

The staff Ticket, or CustomerTicketOnBehalfResult under tickets:act_as_customer

application/json · Ticket | CustomerTicketOnBehalfResult
401

Not authenticated (unauthenticated)

application/problem+json · Problem
Error format and example
403

Visible but not allowed (forbidden, csrf): missing role for the route group, PAT without the operation's x-scopes, or a cookie mutation without a valid CSRF token

application/problem+json · Problem
Error format and example
404

Not found or not visible to the caller (not-found). Portal routes answer 404 to staff and agent/admin routes answer 404 to customers. portal-disabled: the customer portal is switched off (support.portal_enabled=false), so customer sign-in endpoints and the /portal/* group answer 404 to customers (a customer personal access token gets 404 there and 401 elsewhere)

application/problem+json · Problem
Error format and example
409

Conflict (conflict, invalid-transition, merge-cross-requester, link-cycle, email-disabled, setup-required, idempotency-in-flight: a request with the same Idempotency-Key is still running)

application/problem+json · Problem
Error format and example
422

Validation failed (validation, field-required, idempotency-mismatch)

application/problem+json · Problem
Error format and example
429

Too many requests (rate-limited)

application/problem+json · Problem
Headers: Retry-After
Error format and example

Request

curl -X POST 'https://help.example.com/api/v1/agent/tickets' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer fd_pat_…' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"subject":"VPN drops every 10 minutes","body_md":"Since this morning the VPN disconnects every ten minutes.","requester_id":"0192f3c4-5b6a-7c8d-9e0f-1a2b3c4d5e6f","requester_email":"ada@example.com","requester_name":"Acme Support","category_id":"0192f3c4-5b6a-7c8d-9e0f-1a2b3c4d5e6f","team_id":"0192f3c4-5b6a-7c8d-9e0f-1a2b3c4d5e6f","priority":"low","assignee_id":"0192f3c4-5b6a-7c8d-9e0f-1a2b3c4d5e6f","attachment_ids":["0192f3c4-5b6a-7c8d-9e0f-1a2b3c4d5e6f"],"custom_fields":{"order_id":"A-10293"},"tags":["vpn"],"project_id":"0192f0c4-7a1e-7c3e-9a10-4b5f0e2d8a11"}'

PATCH/api/v1/agent/tickets/{id}#

Update ticket fields

auth: token or sessiontickets:writeStaff

Each changed field is authorised separately. Invalid status changes → 409 invalid-transition with allowed.

Parameters

NameInTypeDescription
idrequiredpathstring

UUIDv7

If-Matchheaderstring

ETag of the ticket (updated_at); 412 on conflict

Request body · application/json · required

FieldTypeDescription
statusTicketStatus
one of: new, open, pending, on_hold, resolved, closed
priorityPriority
one of: low, normal, high, urgent
category_idstring | null
team_idstring | null
assignee_idstring | null
subjectstring
min length 1 · max length 200
tagsstring[]
custom_fieldsCustomFieldValues

Map of field key → value. Customer views contain only customer_visible fields.

project_idstring

Move the ticket to another project (id or key). Needs transfer; agents must be members of the target. The ticket gets the next ref of the target project (the old ref no longer resolves; number is unchanged), a category of the old project is cleared, a team not serving the target is replaced by the target's default team (or triage), and the SLA is recomputed with the target's policies. Writes ticket.project_changed.

max length 36

Responses

200

OK

application/json · TicketUpdateResult
401

Not authenticated (unauthenticated)

application/problem+json · Problem
Error format and example
403

Visible but not allowed (forbidden, csrf): missing role for the route group, PAT without the operation's x-scopes, or a cookie mutation without a valid CSRF token

application/problem+json · Problem
Error format and example
404

Not found or not visible to the caller (not-found). Portal routes answer 404 to staff and agent/admin routes answer 404 to customers. portal-disabled: the customer portal is switched off (support.portal_enabled=false), so customer sign-in endpoints and the /portal/* group answer 404 to customers (a customer personal access token gets 404 there and 401 elsewhere)

application/problem+json · Problem
Error format and example
409

Conflict (conflict, invalid-transition, merge-cross-requester, link-cycle, email-disabled, setup-required, idempotency-in-flight: a request with the same Idempotency-Key is still running)

application/problem+json · Problem
Error format and example
412

If-Match did not match (precondition-failed)

application/problem+json · Problem
Error format and example
422

Validation failed (validation, field-required, idempotency-mismatch)

application/problem+json · Problem
Error format and example

POST/api/v1/agent/tickets/{id}/customer-messages#

Post a customer reply on the customer's behalf (integrations)

auth: token or sessiontickets:act_as_customerStaff

For a trusted integration that owns the customer-facing UI. Needs a token that explicitly holds tickets:act_as_customer; a session or the admin scope is never enough (403).

The reply goes through the same path as a portal reply (createPortalReply), with on_behalf_of as the author: pending/on_hold → open, a resolved ticket reopens inside the reopen window, a reply to a closed ticket (or a resolved one past the window) creates a follow-up ticket and the message lives there (followup_ticket). First-response SLA, notifications, the message.created event (actor = the customer) and webhooks (data.message.via_integration: true) are those of a customer reply. set_status: resolved additionally marks the ticket resolved, as the customer could (409 invalid-transition otherwise; ignored when a follow-up is created). The message is always public: a kind other than public is 422.

Checks: unknown ticket or on_behalf_of → 404; a staff user → 403 on-behalf-not-customer; a disabled customer → 409 on-behalf-disabled; a customer who cannot see the ticket → 403 on-behalf-not-visible. attachment_ids must be drafts uploaded by the token's owner (422). Every write is audited (ticket.message.on_behalf, actor = the token owner) and limited to 60 per minute per token (burst 20, 429). status in the answer is the customer status label.

Parameters

NameInTypeDescription
idrequiredpathstring

UUIDv7

Idempotency-Keyheaderstring

Replays within 24 h return the original response; a different body with the same key → 422 idempotency-mismatch

max length 200

UUIDv7

min length 1 · max length 65536

max items 10
set_statusstring
one of: resolved

POST/api/v1/agent/tickets/{id}/macros/{macro_id}/apply#

Apply a macro to a ticket

auth: token or sessiontickets:writeStaff

Applies the macro as the caller in one transaction: the reply or note, then priority, tags, assignee and status. Every part is authorised like the matching single action (allowed_actions): one forbidden part rejects the whole macro with 403 and nothing changes. An invalid status edge is a 409 invalid-transition.

GET/api/v1/agent/projects#

My projects

auth: token or sessiontickets:readdirectory:readStaff

The projects the caller works in: every project for supervisors and admins, the memberships for agents. Inactive projects are included (active: false) so chips of old tickets render. Feeds the project switcher, which is hidden while only one active project exists.

Responses

200

OK

application/json · AgentProject[]
401

Not authenticated (unauthenticated)

application/problem+json · Problem
Error format and example
403

Visible but not allowed (forbidden, csrf): missing role for the route group, PAT without the operation's x-scopes, or a cookie mutation without a valid CSRF token

application/problem+json · Problem
Error format and example
404

Not found or not visible to the caller (not-found). Portal routes answer 404 to staff and agent/admin routes answer 404 to customers. portal-disabled: the customer portal is switched off (support.portal_enabled=false), so customer sign-in endpoints and the /portal/* group answer 404 to customers (a customer personal access token gets 404 there and 401 elsewhere)

auth: token or sessionadminAdmins (some admin routes also allow supervisors or project admins — see the description)

Request body · application/json · required

FieldTypeDescription
namerequiredstring
min length 1 · max length 120
descriptionstring
notification_emailstring (email) | null
notify_modeNotifyMode
one of: agents, mailbox, both
calendar_idstring | null
assignment_strategyAssignmentStrategy

How unassigned tickets of a team get an owner. manual (default) leaves them unassigned; round_robin rotates over the eligible agents; least_busy picks the eligible agent with the fewest open tickets. Eligible = (active, member of the team, effective tier ≥ ticket tier) and not away. It runs on create, team change, escalation or de-escalation that clears the assignee, and unassign.

one of: manual, round_robin, least_busy
project_idsstring[]

Projects the team serves (ids or keys). Omitted on create: the default project; omitted on PATCH: unchanged.

Responses

201

OK

application/json · Team
401

Not authenticated (unauthenticated)

application/problem+json · Problem
Error format and example
403

Visible but not allowed (forbidden, csrf): missing role for the route group, PAT without the operation's x-scopes, or a cookie mutation without a valid CSRF token

application/problem+json · Problem
Error format and example
404

Not found or not visible to the caller (not-found). Portal routes answer 404 to staff and agent/admin routes answer 404 to customers. portal-disabled: the customer portal is switched off (support.portal_enabled=false), so customer sign-in endpoints and the /portal/* group answer 404 to customers (a customer personal access token gets 404 there and 401 elsewhere)

application/problem+json · Problem
Error format and example
409

Conflict (conflict, invalid-transition, merge-cross-requester, link-cycle, email-disabled, setup-required, idempotency-in-flight: a request with the same Idempotency-Key is still running)

application/problem+json · Problem
Error format and example
422

Validation failed (validation, field-required, idempotency-mismatch)

application/problem+json · Problem
Error format and example

Request

curl -X POST 'https://help.example.com/api/v1/admin/teams' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer fd_pat_…' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"Ada Lovelace","description":"Customers of the web shop","notification_email":"ada@example.com","notify_mode":"agents","calendar_id":"0192f3c4-5b6a-7c8d-9e0f-1a2b3c4d5e6f","assignment_strategy":"manual","project_ids":["0192f0c4-7a1e-7c3e-9a10-4b5f0e2d8a11"]}'

POST/api/v1/admin/automation/rules#

Create an automation rule

auth: token or sessionadminAdmins (some admin routes also allow supervisors or project admins — see the description)

Supervisor or admin; a project admin may create rules with the project_id of one of their projects (, a project rule only runs on tickets of that project). The new rule is appended at the end of the order. Conditions hours_since_update and hours_since_status are only valid for event: time, and a time rule needs at least one of them.

Request body · application/json · required

FieldTypeDescription
namerequiredstring
min length 1 · max length 120
eventrequiredAutomationEvent

What runs the rule. message.created fires on customer replies only. ticket.updated fires once per change (status, priority, assignee, team, tier, category, tags, custom fields, subject), never for changes made by automation itself (loop guard). time rules run on the hourly scheduler.

one of: ticket.created, message.created, ticket.updated, time
matchAutomationMatch
one of: all, any
conditionsAutomationCondition[]
max items 20
conditions[].fieldrequiredAutomationConditionField
one of: subject, body, channel, priority, status, tier, category_id, team_id, project, organization_id, requester_domain, tag, …
conditions[].oprequiredAutomationOperator

Allowed per field: subject/body contains, not_contains, regex (RE2, ≤ 500 characters, case-insensitive); channel/priority/status/category_id/team_id/organization_id/requester_domain is, is_not (a value or a list); tier is, is_not, gte, lte; tag present, absent; custom_field equals, contains (needs key); business_hours is (boolean); hours_since_update/hours_since_status gte (time rules only).

one of: is, is_not, contains, not_contains, regex, gte, lte, present, absent, equals
conditions[].keystring

Custom field key (custom_field only)

conditions[].valuestring | number | boolean | array
actionsrequiredAutomationAction[]
min items 1 · max items 10
actions[].typerequiredAutomationActionType
one of: set_priority, set_team, set_category, set_status, set_tier, add_tag, remove_tag, assign, add_note, send_reply, escalate, add_watcher
actions[].valuestring | integer

Priority, team id, category id (empty = none), status, tier or tag name

actions[].strategystring

assign with a strategy

one of: round_robin, least_busy
actions[].user_idId

assign to a specific agent, add_watcher

actions[].body_mdstring

add_note text (internal, never shown to customers)

max length 10000
actions[].canned_response_idId

send_reply: the canned response sent as a public reply

enabledboolean
stop_processingboolean
project_idstring | null

the rule only runs for tickets of this project; null = every project (supervisors and admins only)

Created

PATCH/api/v1/admin/settings#

Update support settings

auth: token or sessionadminAdmins (some admin routes also allow supervisors or project admins — see the description)

Request body · application/json · required

FieldTypeDescription
tier_labelsobject
tier_labels.1string
tier_labels.2string
tier_labels.3string
auto_close_daysinteger
≥ 0
reopen_window_daysinteger
≥ 0
self_registrationboolean
customer_urgent_allowedboolean
urgent_requires_supervisorboolean
triage_visible_to_agentsboolean
portal_enabledboolean

Customer portal switch (default true). false leaves only admin and staff sign-in: the portal web routes redirect to /agent/login, customer sign-in, registration, magic link, invite acceptance, and customer OIDC answer 404 portal-disabled, /portal/* answers 404 to customers, customer personal access tokens stop working (401, or 404 under /portal/), customer WebSockets close with 4403 and existing customer sessions are revoked when it is switched off. Emails to customers, inbound email replies and tickets created by staff on a customer's behalf keep working. The public knowledge base follows its own kb_enabled.

kb_enabledboolean
kb_sitemap_enabledboolean
default_localeLocale
one of: en, it, de, fr, es

POST/api/v1/me/privacy/export#

Request an export of my data

auth: token or sessionadmin

Starts an asynchronous export job (data subject access, GDPR art. 15/20). The ZIP holds JSON files (profile, tickets as requester, the caller's messages, attachment metadata and files, consent records, audit entries about the caller) and is downloadable for retention.export_days (default 7) from GET /me/privacy/exports/{id}; an email is sent when it is ready. Customers never receive internal notes, staff-only fields or other customers' messages. 409 while another export is pending.

Responses

202

Export queued

401

POST/api/v1/admin/privacy/users/{id}/erase#

Erase a user

auth: token or sessionadminAdmins (some admin routes also allow supervisors or project admins — see the description)

Irreversible. anonymize: the name becomes "Deleted user #n", the email erased+<id>@invalid; identities, sessions, tokens, MFA, notifications, the signature and preferences are removed and the user is disabled. anonymize_and_redact also replaces the bodies of messages the user wrote with [redacted], deletes the user's attachments (rows and files) and the custom-field values and CSAT comments of tickets they requested, and refreshes the search index. Tickets stay (business records). Pending erasure requests of the user are completed. 409 for the caller themselves, a break-glass admin, or the last active admin.

POST/mcp#

MCP endpoint (Streamable HTTP)

auth: token or session

Model Context Protocol server for AI clients (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, …): one JSON-RPC 2.0 message per POST, answered with a single JSON body (never an SSE stream). Off unless an admin sets integrations.mcp_enabled (PATCH /admin/integrations); while off every /mcp method answers 404. Guide: docs/features/mcp.md.

Authentication. Authorization: Bearer fd_pat_… only; cookies are ignored. Every tool runs as the token owner, limited by the token's scopes, as an in-process call of the matching REST operation, so it gets exactly that operation's x-scopes, authorisation, lifecycle checks and customer-safe view. Customers' tokens get customer tools only. A request with an Origin header other than the public URL's origin (or one in FD_ALLOWED_ORIGINS) is refused with 403 (DNS rebinding). Rate limits: 20/s per client IP and 10/s (burst 40) per token owner.

Protocol revisions. 2026-07-28 (stateless: _meta.io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion and clientCapabilities on every request, mirrored in MCP-Protocol-Version, Mcp-Method and Mcp-Name; server/discover; header mismatch → 400 -32020, unsupported version → 400 -32022, unknown method → 404 -32601) and the session-based 2025-11-25, 2025-06-18 and 2025-03-26 (initialize returns Mcp-Session-Id, required on every later request: missing → 400, unknown or expired → 404; JSON-RPC batches only in a 2025-03-26 session). Methods: initialize, ping, server/discover, tools/list, tools/call, resources/list, resources/templates/list, resources/read.

Tools: search_tickets, list_my_tickets, get_ticket, create_ticket, reply_to_ticket, update_ticket, search_kb, get_kb_article, list_categories, and for staff also add_internal_note, escalate_ticket, deescalate_ticket, apply_macro, list_teams. Tool failures are results with isError: true and the REST problem slug in structuredContent.error.slug. Resources: ticket://{number}, kb://{slug}.

Parameters

NameInTypeDescription
MCP-Protocol-Versionheaderstring

Protocol revision of the request (required by 2025-06-18 and later after initialize)

Mcp-Session-Idheaderstring

Legacy session from initialize (2025-03-26 … 2025-11-25); ignored by 2026-07-28

Mcp-Methodheaderstring

2026-07-28: mirrors the JSON-RPC method

Mcp-Nameheaderstring

2026-07-28: mirrors params.name (tools/call) or params.uri (resources/read)

idstring | integer
methodstring
paramsobject

Start the Slack install (OAuth popup)

auth: token or sessionadminAdmins (some admin routes also allow supervisors or project admins — see the description)

Returns Slack's consent URL with a single-use state (10 minutes, bound to the caller). The SPA opens it in a popup; Slack then redirects to GET /integrations/slack/oauth/callback. 409 conflict until the app credentials are saved.

GET/api/v1/integrations/slack/oauth/callback#

Slack OAuth redirect target

public

The redirect URL registered in the Slack app. Authenticated by state alone (single use), not by a session. Exchanges code for the bot token (oauth.v2.access), stores it sealed and audits slack.connected. Always answers 302 to <FD_AGENT_URL>/oauth/complete?provider=slack&state=…&result=ok|error[&reason=<code>], the page that tells the admin's window and closes the popup. Reasons include invalid_state, access_denied, no_bot_token, enterprise_install_unsupported and Slack error codes such as bad_client_secret.

Parameters

NameInTypeDescription
codequerystring
statequerystring
errorquerystring

Responses

302

Redirect to the SPA completion page

429

Too many requests (rate-limited)

application/problem+json · Problem
Headers: Retry-After
Error format and example

Request

Webhooks

Admins register webhook URLs under Administration → Webhooks and pick events. FeatherDesk sends a POST with a JSON envelope; delivery is at least once (deduplicate on the envelope id), failed deliveries are retried with back-off, and a webhook is disabled after 20 consecutive failures or a 410 Gone.

HeaderValue
X-FeatherDesk-EventThe event type, e.g. ticket.created
X-FeatherDesk-DeliveryUnique delivery id (UUID)
X-FeatherDesk-Signaturet=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256(secret, t + "." + body)>. Recompute it with the webhook's secret, compare in constant time and reject timestamps older than 5 minutes.
